facts.text: I've been short of breath.
It has been getting steadily worse.
I've been coughing.

facts.item: when the breathlessness and cough started
facts.text: Both started six weeks ago.
I passed out once, during a coughing attack.
It kept building up until I had a severe coughing attack.

facts.item: swelling of the face and neck
facts.text: My face and neck are very swollen.

facts.item: blood in the whites of the eyes
facts.text: There's blood in the whites of both my eyes.
At first I was told I probably had allergic asthma.

facts.item: response to the asthma and allergy treatment
facts.text: I was treated with inhalers to open my airways, steroid tablets and antihistamines, and none of it helped.
I spent 14 days in a local hospital before I was sent here.
I smoked, about 5 pack-years, and I quit when these symptoms started.
I'm allergic to dust mites, pollen, hay, straw, cats and dogs.
I take prednisolone 25 mg a day.
I take levocetirizine when I need it.
I use a budesonide inhaler.
I use a fenoterol/ipratropium bromide inhaler when I need it.
I take dihydrocodeine.
I use a nicotine patch.
I've been told I have thrush in my voice box.
I'm using a local antifungal treatment for the thrush.

findings.name: CT of the head, neck, chest and abdomen
repeat chest CT
findings.result: Peribronchovascular ground-glass opacities in the mediobasal segment of the left lower lobe; minimal tree-in-bud opacities in the left upper lobe.

findings.name: respiratory pathogen serology
findings.result: Respiratory syncytial virus, coxsackievirus, echovirus, adenovirus, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Legionella pneumophila and Mycoplasma pneumoniae: negative.

gold.reasoning: 1. Allergic histamine-mediated angioedema was considered but excluded because “the clinical symptoms as well as the treatment resistance to antihistamines and steroids made allergic, histamine-mediated angioedema unlikely.” 2. ACE-inhibitor–induced angioedema was ruled out since “the patient had never taken ACE-inhibitors, which ruled out ACE-inhibitor induced angioedema.” 3. Hypothyroid myxedema was excluded because “normal thyroid function was not suggestive of myxoedema.” 4. Cushing’s disease was excluded as “cortisol and ACTH levels were within the normal range and thus did not support Cushing’s disease.” 5. Superior vena cava syndrome and right heart failure were ruled out based on imaging and echocardiography: “Superior vena cava syndrome and right heart failure were also ruled out.” 6. Lymphoproliferative disorders were investigated but “no evidence of lymphoma or other malignancies were found.” 7. Autoimmune conditions were considered, but “the combination of the clinical presentation and complement factor and autoantibody testing were not suggestive of an underlying autoimmune disease.” 8. Common respiratory infections were excluded since “serologies for respiratory syncytial virus, coxsackievirus, echovirus, adenovirus, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Legionella pneumophila and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were negative.”

f002: 'progressive dyspnea and coughing': 'progressive' is read with the breathlessness; the cough's course is that it culminated in a severe attack (f006).
f007: The swelling is the 'angioedema' of the referral reason (s001) and the examination (s004); worded as what the patient sees.
f008: Patient-noticeable sign taken from the examination (subconjunctival hemorrhages).
f018: The reason for dihydrocodeine is not given (probably cough suppression).

x003: The examiner's obesity is from 160 cm and 85 kg; no BMI is given.
x010: s008 and s012 both describe CT of the head, neck and chest; whether s012 is a separate study is unclear, so x021 is kept as the hematology CT that adds the abdomen.
x022: '13 days later' has no stated reference point (probably the first CT).
x024: The individual autoantibodies tested are not listed.

source_issues: s013: 'Repeat chest CT 13 days later' does not say what it is later than.
s008 and s012 may describe the same CT of the head, neck and chest.
No Bordetella pertussis test (PCR, culture or serology) is reported in the prompt.
notes: Index visit: the referral visit for therapy-resistant breathlessness and facial swelling after six weeks of illness and 14 days in a local hospital (s001, s004-s006); the earlier illness and treatment (s002, s003) are history, and all tests (s007-s017) are findings from the referral workup.
s003: the earlier asthma/allergy treatment is one response fact (f010); the drugs she is still taking are listed one per fact from s006.
s012: 'Because of the marked lymphocytosis, hematology evaluated for lymphoproliferative disease' is clinician reasoning and is not used; the test results in that sentence are findings.
A doctor requesting a pertussis test gets no result: none is reported.
